causal_graphs.context: 225 ug enzyme, 46 mM each MEP and CTP, 10 mM MgCl2, 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 0.7 ml, 37 C for 1 h; HPLC purification and NMR product identification.

evidence.explanation: Preparation Methods, Table 2 and recombinant-product Results establish the adopted endpoint; Figure 4 supports purification scope.
Exact current reference mapping; identity evidence is not an additional causal experiment.

edges.mechanism: The joint preparative reaction yields CDP-ME. Its agreement with the independently characterized partial-preparation product supports this chemical endpoint without resolving each phosphate-transfer microstep.
edges.subject: purified-ispd-with-mep-ctp-magnesium

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q46893/ISPD_ECOLI, ispD/ygbP/b2747, 236-aa K12 reference, sequence version 3; PF01128 spans 8-229. UniProt and InterPro sequences match. The paper reports initiator-methionine removal and an N-terminal sequence consistent with ygbP. Exact donor strain and complete plasmid sequence are not independently resolved.
causal_graphs.limitations: NMR supports product identity, not a directly observed transition state. Raw spectra and preparative replicate/control details remain unverified. Partial-preparation nucleotide promiscuity, recombinant coupled-assay signals and plant label incorporation are not equivalent experiments or independently identified products.

nodes.label: Purified IspD with MEP, CTP and magnesium

causal_graphs.scope: Recombinant ygbP from pNCOygbP in XL1-blue, purified in the 1999 study. This is an intact enzyme assay, not an isolated Pfam fragment or a plant pathway experiment.
causal_graphs.title: Purified E. coli IspD produces CDP-ME

causal_graphs.context: Pulse 2 mM labeled CTP with 2.2 mM enzyme, then chase with 10 mM each CTP/MEP, 100 mM Tris pH 8, 10 mM MgCl2, 2 mM DTT and 4.48 U pyrophosphatase. Compare label-in-pulse with label-in-chase control at early sampled times; TLC/phosphorimaging. Methods uses room-temperature preincubation and 5-s sampling.

evidence.explanation: Primary proof pages D/E, Figure 3B and control Methods support the early-product comparison; the quotation is the authors' interpretation, not an additional observed step.

edges.mechanism: The CTP-pulse curve rises ahead of the matched label-in-chase control. This is a controlled isotope-trapping effect, not an exact binding fraction, equilibrium Kd or observed atomic trajectory.
edges.subject: labeled-ctp-in-pulse

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The cited construct-source structure 1I52 entity 1 exactly matches Q46893's 236-aa sequence, including PF01128 at 8-229. pHIS8-ygbP is expressed in BL21(DE3), then tag-cleaved for purified assays. Exact cleavage remnant and every later clone sequence remain unverified.
causal_graphs.limitations: The inspected copy has lettered proof pages and placeholder publication fields; final tables/figures were not compared. Figure 3's percent-axis scale conflicts with the prose's trapped fraction, so only direction is retained. A 40-s displayed series differs from the 50-s Methods duration. Isotope trapping supports the authors' ordered-binding interpretation but does not directly image binding or prove that MEP can never associate first.

nodes.label: Put labeled CTP in the enzyme pulse rather than the chase
Early labeled CDP-ME formation after addition of both substrates

causal_graphs.scope: Purified, thrombin-cleaved E. coli YgbP in the 2004 primary proof's Figure 3B pulse-chase comparison; not the distinct MEP-pulse experiment.
causal_graphs.title: CTP preloading increases early labeled CDP-ME formation

causal_graphs.context: TLC product kinetics at 23 C; 5 ul with 398 nmol Tris-HCl, 40 nmol MgCl2, 79 nmol NaOH and 0.7 U pyrophosphatase; 6/12-min sampling. CTP varies, MEP is fixed separately for each mutant. Table 1 uses a CTP-inhibition fit, plus MEP-unsaturation corrections for T140V/R109A. At least two independent assay sets; variable protein doses keep consumption below 10%.

evidence.explanation: Proof page F, K27S and WT CTP columns; purification and kinetic Methods on page D. Figure 5 instead uses the corrected MEP comparison.

edges.mechanism: Table 1 reports K27S at 2.05 versus WT 54.1 per second in the CTP series. Residual activity is retained; neither absolute inactivity nor a unique lysine chemical role is asserted.
edges.subject: k27s-purified

evidence.explanation: Proof page F, D106E and WT CTP columns; substantial between-run uncertainty is retained in the assessment.

edges.mechanism: D106E has lower reported CTP-series turnover than WT, 0.93 versus 54.1 per second. This does not directly establish which binding, conformational or chemical step changed.
edges.subject: d106e-purified

evidence.explanation: Proof page F, T140V row and footnote c; the separate T104V wording discrepancy remains unresolved.

edges.mechanism: The T140V row gives corrected CTP-series turnover of 1.8 versus WT 54.1 per second. The additional correction for unsaturating MEP is part of this estimate, not an independently observed catalytic constant.
edges.subject: t140v-purified

evidence.explanation: Proof page F, R109A CTP column and footnote c; distinct from the MEP-series estimate.

edges.mechanism: Corrected R109A CTP-series turnover is 0.26 versus WT 54.1 per second. The measured product kinetics and model correction support a decrease, not a directly observed hydrogen-bond network or universal binding defect.
edges.subject: r109a-purified

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q46893 and 1I52 canonical sequences match; PF01128 spans 8-229 and contains K27, D106, R109 and T140. The experiments concern full-length enzyme from pHIS8-ygbP, not independent sufficiency of those residues or the isolated domain.
causal_graphs.limitations: These are reported fitted parameters, not direct binding affinities or observed transition-state stabilization. Final assay pH and complete clones remain unverified. Between-run variation, excluded fit outliers and substrate-inhibition corrections matter. The proof footnote says T104V where the main row says T140V; K27S's corrected MEP and CTP values differ and are not silently averaged. Final publication comparison remains open.

D106E instead of WT in purified kinetics
T140V instead of WT in purified kinetics
R109A instead of WT in purified kinetics
Reported CTP-series turnover from labeled CDP-ME kinetics

causal_graphs.scope: K27S, D106E, T140V and R109A versus WT in the 2004 proof's purified, tag-cleaved preparations. Inactive unpurified mutants belong to a separate graph.
causal_graphs.title: Purified IspD substitutions lower reported CTP-series turnover

causal_graphs.context: 217 nmol labeled MEP, 81.3 nmol CTP, 400 nmol Tris-HCl, 40 nmol MgCl2, 79 nmol NaOH and a nominal 1-ug YgbP-containing crude sample in 5 ul; 23 C, 1/15 h. TLC background from a blank lacking YgbP is subtracted. Exact protein-normalization basis and final assay pH remain unresolved.

evidence.explanation: Proof page E crude-extract Results and page F Table 1; not a purified D106A kinetic measurement.

edges.mechanism: D106A gives no detected product activity relative to the active WT screen; this does not isolate an elementary chemical defect.
edges.subject: d106a-crude

evidence.explanation: Proof page E crude-extract Results and page F Table 1; no purified D106N curve is claimed.

edges.mechanism: D106N gives no detected product activity in this extract comparison; abundance and folding are not excluded as contributors.
edges.subject: d106n-crude

evidence.explanation: Proof page E screen and page F Table 1, with the no-further-purification qualification.

edges.mechanism: K213S lowers detected extract product formation below the screen's reported activity detection; charge stabilization is an interpretation, not the measured endpoint.
edges.subject: k213s-crude

evidence.explanation: Proof page E and Table 1 distinguish K27A screening from the separately purified K27S mutant.

edges.mechanism: K27A has no detected extract activity in the screen. It is not conflated with K27S, which retains purified activity.
edges.subject: k27a-crude

evidence.explanation: Proof page E describes inclusion bodies and screen results; Table 1's inactive label is not a purified turnover fit.

edges.mechanism: T165V gives no detected extract activity. Its aggregation qualification prevents assigning the entire decrease to a particular substrate contact.
edges.subject: t165v-crude

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Intended substitutions map to Q46893's PF01128 interval 8-229; the cited 1I52 reference sequence matches. Unlike purified kinetics, the crude screen precedes His8-tag cleavage. Complete mutant clone sequences are not independently verified.
causal_graphs.limitations: No activity was detected under the reported screen, not proven chemically impossible under all conditions. Directness is UNRESOLVED because expression, soluble yield, folding and background enzymes can contribute. D106/T165 variants partly form inclusion bodies. The source's sensitivity estimate does not supply independent mutant-specific detection limits or folded-protein controls. Proof-only full-text access remains explicit.

nodes.label: Detected labeled CDP-ME formation in the crude-extract screen

causal_graphs.scope: BL21(DE3) extracts expressing D106A, D106N, K213S, K27A or T165V, compared with WT, in the 2004 proof. These variants were not further purified. PHENOTYPIC denotes the biochemical assay effect without a resolved molecular cause.
causal_graphs.title: Five IspD substitutions reduce crude-extract CDP-ME production
